text:
devon: alert: sudden throughput drop on infer-prod-dedicated pool (p50->p99 latency spike, requests queuing) :rotating_light:
anne: seeing the same. dashboards show worker restarts and OOMs on GPU nodes. p50 ~120ms -> 700ms, p99 ~2.1s -> 9s
raj: @devon can you paste the nvidia-smi / dmesg snippet? might be mem fragmentation, or model KV cache thrash.
devon: attaching quick logs:
```
Nov 10 03:12:17 worker-3 runtime[pid]: GPU 0: CUDA OOM while allocating 1.2GiB
Nov 10 03:12:18 worker-3 runtime[pid]: kernel_selector: fallback to generic-kernel (mem-saver) after OOM
Nov 10 03:12:19 worker-3 runtime[pid]: kv_cache: evicted 42 prefixes (total 3.9GiB)
Nov 10 03:12:21 worker-3 systemd[1]: runtime.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```
raj: looks like a noisy tenant pushed large contexts, causing KV cache churn, then kernel fallback and restarts. the fallback kernels are slower -> latency spike.
tara: also seeing high batching sizes at the time: batching heuristic allowed 48 concurrent contexts on that host; memory peaked.
anne: confirmed — batching behaviour: heuristic increased batch cap after short latency dip, then memory rose and fragmentation caused OOMs.
sre-oncall-bot: incident created: INC-20231110-42 assigned to eng-runtime + eng-sre, severity: high
devon: mitigation plan: (1) cordon noisy node and drain (2) set KG_KERNEL_POLICY=mem-conservative on pool for rollback (3) reduce max_batch_size env to 32 as emergency cap (4) bump KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD down to 0.6 to evict earlier
raj: quick test: can we change the kernel selection order to prefer int8/quantized kernels for long contexts? that would reduce peak allocation.
tara: we only have quantized variants for some models; for others fallback still required. short-term kernel-policy override is fastest.
anne: applied env change on two nodes, rolling restart started (rolling 2 at a time). monitoring...
devon: after first roll: p50=180ms, p99=1.4s, throughput recovering ~70% of normal. no new OOMs logged.
raj: added a perf profile dump command to collector, can you check the kernel hotpath sample?
devon: profiler snippet:
```
hotpath: aten_attn_kernel_mem_opt (42%)
next: generic_attn_loop (18%)
alloc/free churn: 310k ops, avg alloc 24KiB
```
raj: allocator churn confirms fragmentation — frequent small allocs between attention calls. long-term we should: (a) add a pre-alloc slab for attention KV to reduce fragmentation, (b) make batching heuristic memory-aware (cap by estimated per-request memory usage), (c) expose kernel policy per-model to avoid global fallbacks.
tara: creating follow-up tickets: RUNTIME-482 (slab prealloc), RUNTIME-483 (memory-aware batching), RUNTIME-484 (per-model kernel policy).
devon: action items for now: anne/raj keep draining noisy node, tara coord with infra to add capacity spike for dedicated pool, devon to run postmortem once stabilized. /cc @eng-runtime @eng-sre
anne: noting timeline, will add minimal chronology to incident doc.
sre-oncall-bot: incident update: mitigations applied, status: stabilizing, next update in 30m.
deploy-bot: rollback of new batching heuristic scheduled? none detected in last deploy window. no rollbacks triggered.
devon: initial RCA summary (to expand in postmortem): noisy tenant sent a burst of large-context requests that triggered KV cache evictions, allocator fragmentation and CUDA OOMs; fallback kernel policy caused slower kernels and worker restarts -> throughput drop. Immediate fix: per-pool kernel override + batch cap + node drainage. Long-term: allocator slab, memory-aware batching and per-model kernel policy.
raj: will attach perf traces and allocator heap dumps to the incident doc.
tara: thanks team. I'll schedule a deep-dive with eng-runtime next week to prioritize the three follow-ups. :calendar:
